findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 publishes 'WeirdML v3' and lists only 'Previous versions: WeirdML v2 · WeirdML v1'. The row claims version 2, version_status 'published', status 'active', and version_guard 'Verify the published version 2 before reading results.' The current protocol's release identifier is v3, not v2, and no v2 protocol excerpt is supplied, so the claimed current version/identity cannot be established.
findings.repair: Either set version to 3 and update the row to the current v3 protocol, or treat the row as retained/superseded v2 and supply the v2 protocol evidence that defines its identity and scoring.

findings.evidence: Row scoring.metric is 'Average Max Accuracy: per task, mean over runs of the maximum test accuracy across the 5 iterations per run, averaged over all 17 tasks'. SOURCE 1 says WeirdML v3 has '11 complex hand-made tasks' and official score is '80% normalized area under its line ... plus 20% of its final value', and 'Effective scores ... are not raw accuracy'. This contradicts the supplied current protocol; SOURCE 3 only establishes the numeric scale of avg_acc, not metric meaning.
findings.repair: Replace the metric with the current v3 scoring rule and 11-task scope, or capture and verify the v2 protocol that defines the 17-task/5-iteration maximum-accuracy metric.

findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 names 'WeirdML v3' as the current version and places v2 under 'Previous versions', which names v3 as the successor board. The row sets superseded_by null. Under c2, a named successor contradicts null; SOURCE 2's nonzero changed-value count can support status active but does not settle supersession.
findings.repair: Set superseded_by to the registry id for WeirdML v3, or provide protocol evidence that v2 has no successor board.

findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 describes v3 as an agentic benchmark with 11 tasks, developing ML/data-analysis pipelines under limited data and feedback. The excerpt does not mention PyTorch code, fixed compute/time limits, or 'write, run, and iteratively improve', so the row description is unsupported for v2 and not a description of the supplied v3 protocol.
findings.repair: Align the description with the captured protocol excerpt, or add the v2 protocol text that supports the claimed description.

uncertainties: SOURCE 2 and SOURCE 3 do not state whether their avg_acc payload is for WeirdML v2 or v3; I treated them as evidence for row weirdml::2's source field, but they cannot settle metric meaning or version.
I could not execute SHA-256 or transport/qualification checks; those are owner-controlled checks.
The absence of a dedicated v2 page makes it ambiguous whether the metric/description mismatches are wrong-value failures or missing-evidence failures.
missing_evidence: WeirdML v2 protocol text or page: task count, scoring rule covering '5 iterations' and 'maximum test accuracy', description, and whether v2 remains published; SOURCE 1 contains only the v3 page and a one-line 'Previous versions: WeirdML v2' link.
